newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips as spot demand dries up.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips as spot demand dries up.

text.p: French wheat prices eased on Thursday on dwindling demand for spot grain, dealers said.
Demand for spot wheat had helped to underpin French wheat in recent days amid a tight situation in French port silos.
"The fever has come down," one dealer said.
Wheat into Rouen for December delivery was quoted at 845 francs per tonne, down five on Wednesday.
Wheat into Rouen for January-March delivery fetched 825-830 francs against 835 francs on the previous day.
In France traders asked to export 552,500 tonnes of EU soft wheat at rebates ranging from 12.87 to 22.00 Ecus per tonne at this week's EU grain auction.
The highest demand for rebate was below the 22.35 Ecus subsidy the EU granted last week for wheat exports.

But traders said this was widely expected as firmer world prices have eased pressure for substantial EU subsidy. They calculated that a refund of 16 to 17 Ecus per tonne would allow the EU to maintain its weekly export pace of 300,000 tonnes.

U.S. wheat futures rallied on Wednesday on brighter prospects for wheat exports. Support also came after an EU farm official hinted the EU may scale back export subsidies because of budget problems. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
